## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 10 (*Pathavīkhaṇana*) governs the monastic rule prohibiting Buddhist monks from digging the earth or causing it to be dug by others, an offense requiring confession (*pācittiya*) [SuttaCentral; Dhammika 2005; Schmithausen 1991]. In the Vinaya background, laypeople objected to monastic earth-digging because contemporary societal and ascetic groups (such as the Jains) regarded the earth as a living entity possessing a single sense faculty (*ekindriya jīva*), viewing digging as an act of injury [Buddhism into the Year 2000 1999; Dhammika 2005]. Redaction-historically, modern scholars have observed that the structural sequence of the introductory narrative in Pācittiya 10 closely mirrors other environmental monastic rules, such as Pācittiya 11 regarding plant life, when freed of secondary interpolations [Buddhism into the Year 2000 1999; Schmithausen 1991]. Later monastic guidance literature addresses the practical application of this precept by delineating the allowable limits of hinting to lay followers when ground work or path clearing is required [Dhammika 2005].
Full parallels are widely preserved across Vinaya traditions in Pali, Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan recensions, including corresponding rules in the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (*pli-tv-bi-vb-pc106*) and parallel codes of the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsaṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, and Kāśyapīya traditions [SuttaCentral]. In DharmaNexus text-reuse data, Pācittiya 10 shares extensive phraseology with subsequent Vibhaṅga rules, most notably Pācittiya 11 (5 matches) and Pācittiya 20 (9 matches), as well as subcommentaries including the *Vinayavinicchayaṭīkā* and *Vinayasaṅgaha-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language alignments are registered in the Tibetan *Vinayavibhaṅga* (D0003-4) and Vinayasūtra commentaries [DharmaNexus].
